title: General token (fallback profile)
applies_to: Any project that does not fit a more specific profile: DeFi applications, consumer apps, exchanges and other tokens. Use a specific profile when one fits; scores are only comparable within the same profile version.
origin: Second version, written for cr-research-prompt@5: the thirteen category grades replace the eleven diagnostics of general-token@1. Protocol-risk transparency is no longer a separate category; administrative control and audit scope are read under project legitimacy, and how those controls are operated under build and operational quality. general-token@1 is unchanged and still grades the reports that declare it.
scorecard_note: Thirteen category grades, each 1-100 with higher meaning better quality or opportunity, each with a confidence, the strongest evidence, the main weakness and what would raise or lower it. They are diagnostics: never averaged into the investment grade, which the dashboard calculates from the six weighted components of the grading rubric. Unknown means unknown and carries no number; missing evidence is not automatically evidence of failure.

diagnostic_categories.label: Project legitimacy
diagnostic_categories.definition: Is this the real project, run by an identifiable and accountable organization: an official website, token, chain and contract, documentation, repository, explorer and official X account that link to each other; team and operating history; security incidents; audit scope; governance and administrative control; and no material misrepresentation. An identifiable organization, functioning software and a trustworthy investment are three separate conclusions: this grade covers who runs the project and the honesty of its claims.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: Which independently checkable facts confirm or contradict who runs the project, which token is the real one, and what the project says about itself?

diagnostic_categories.label: Development credibility
diagnostic_categories.definition: Whether real, substantive development is happening in the repositories that actually power the product: recent releases, meaningful code changes, active contributors, reviewed pull requests, issue handling and maintenance, told apart from automated commits, cosmetic activity, promotional repositories and unrelated forks. Stars, followers and commit counts are not evidence.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: Which repositories power the live product, and what substantive changes shipped in them over the last 90 days, from how many distinct contributors?

diagnostic_categories.label: Build and operational quality
diagnostic_categories.definition: How well the product is built and run: architecture, release discipline, documentation, tests, dependency and upgrade management, uptime, incident handling, and how administrative controls are operated.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: How did the team handle its most recent release and its most recent incident, and what do the documentation and tests show about how the product is maintained?

diagnostic_categories.label: Code quality
diagnostic_categories.definition: Quality of representative implementation code inspected at an identified commit: maintainability, tests, dependencies, security-sensitive controls, whether documented features appear implemented, and whether the inspected code can be connected to what is deployed. A research assessment, not a security audit. Unknown when source access is insufficient; an audit badge is not a substitute.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: Which files were inspected at which commit, do they implement what the documentation describes, and can that code be tied to the deployed contracts or binaries?

diagnostic_categories.label: Live product reality
diagnostic_categories.definition: What is live and independently substantiated today, kept apart from project claims, announced or unfinished features, incentivized demonstrations and speculative future uses.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: Which functions can an outside user exercise today, and which independent evidence (on-chain activity, a working product, a third-party integration in use) shows it?

diagnostic_categories.label: Technology usefulness and defensibility
diagnostic_categories.definition: Whether the technology solves a real problem for identifiable users better than credible alternatives, including a centralized service, and whether that advantage is defensible: technical differentiation, centralization dependencies, failure modes, performance, and whether crypto, decentralization and the token are necessary to the product.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: Who needs this, what would they use instead, and what can this project do that its closest competitors and a centralized service cannot?

diagnostic_categories.label: Organic demand and adoption
diagnostic_categories.definition: Usage, customers and revenue that persist net of token incentives, points programs, subsidies, emissions, related-party activity and wash activity, and whether customers stay.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: What paid or unsubsidized usage remains over the last 90 days after excluding incentive-driven, related-party and wash activity?

diagnostic_categories.label: Token value capture
diagnostic_categories.definition: How product success reaches token holders as implemented today (fee share, buyback or burn, required usage, staking funded by real revenue), and how it might not. Announced but unimplemented mechanisms are conditional; emissions are not value capture.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: Which implemented mechanism routes revenue or required demand to the token, and how much has it delivered over a stated period?

diagnostic_categories.label: Valuation and supply attractiveness
diagnostic_categories.definition: Current market cap and fully diluted valuation relative to revenue, usage and peers, after reconciling circulating supply, total supply, liquidity, emissions and the unlock schedule, with the focus on supply entering between the horizon's start and end dates. An unlock is potential liquid supply, not proof of selling.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: What supply enters between the horizon's start and end dates as a share of circulating supply, and how does valuation compare with revenue or usage over a stated period?

diagnostic_categories.label: Chart structure
diagnostic_categories.definition: Quality of the price structure from a named data source, venue, trading pair and timeframe: trend and market structure against USD and BTC, support and resistance, bases, failed breakouts and drawdowns, weekly and daily first. Unknown when reliable chart data is unavailable; levels and patterns are never invented.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: On the weekly and daily charts, is the token holding higher lows against both USD and BTC, and which levels define the structure?

diagnostic_categories.label: Cycle position and catalyst timing
diagnostic_categories.definition: Where the token stands in its own cycle (launch, decline, base formation, possible accumulation, breakout, expansion, distribution or renewed decline), how sector strength, Bitcoin leadership and altcoin participation bear on it, and whether dated catalysts and supply events between the horizon's start and end dates favor a position now. Competing interpretations are explained; a cycle label is not forced.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: Which phase best fits the evidence, what is the competing reading, and which dated catalysts and supply events fall inside the horizon?

diagnostic_categories.label: Volume confirmation and executable liquidity
diagnostic_categories.definition: Whether volume supports or contradicts the price move against an explicitly stated baseline, and whether a spot position can be entered and exited at reasonable cost: spot liquidity, spreads, depth and venue concentration. High reported volume does not prove durable demand; derivatives data is market context only.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: How does recent volume compare with a stated baseline on the main spot venues, and what are the spread and the 2% depth there?

diagnostic_categories.label: BTC-relative asymmetric opportunity
diagnostic_categories.definition: Whether the token offers a credible advantage over simply holding BTC between the horizon's start and end dates: the balance of upside and downside across the bear, base and bull cases, and how much of it rests on observation rather than assumption. Unknown when the asymmetry cannot be assessed; a number is never forced.
diagnostic_categories.resolving_question: What would have to be true for the token to outperform BTC over the horizon, and how much of that is observed today rather than assumed?

research_sections.title: Identity and legitimacy
research_sections.guidance: Who controls upgrades, treasuries, oracles and custody; whether audits cover the code that is deployed; counterparty exposure.

research_sections.title: Development credibility, build quality and code quality
research_sections.guidance: The contracts or services users actually interact with, and whether the public repositories correspond to them.

research_sections.title: Product reality and technology usefulness
research_sections.guidance: How the product works, where funds sit, which parts are on-chain and which are not, who can change the rules, and what users would use instead.

research_sections.title: Demand, token economics and valuation
research_sections.guidance: Keep three things separate: (a) business activity and the fees it earns, (b) income paid to users or liquidity providers and its source, (c) token-holder economics. Organic usage and whether unit economics work without emissions.

research_sections.title: Chart, volume and market cycle
research_sections.guidance: The sector this token trades with, and whether that sector is leading or lagging BTC.

research_sections.title: Independent judgment and asymmetry
research_sections.guidance: What the token is being priced as (its sector narrative) against what its economics support.

economics_fields.label: Business revenue
economics_fields.definition: Fees earned by the protocol or company from its business activity. Not emissions.

economics_fields.label: Usage / volume
economics_fields.definition: Gross activity processed, with definition and period. Volume is not revenue.

economics_fields.label: User or LP yield
economics_fields.definition: Return paid to users or liquidity providers and its source (fees versus incentives).

economics_fields.label: Token-holder distributions
economics_fields.definition: Value actually distributed to or burned for token holders over a stated period. Emissions are not distributions.

economics_fields.label: Incentive spend
economics_fields.definition: Token emissions or grants spent to attract usage over a stated period.
